[0] As early as next month, Apple is expected to unveil a redesigned next-generation MacBook Pro. Expect to see an OLED display, the first touchscreen in the Mac lineup, a thinner body, Dynamic Island, and more. There were earlier rumours that the upgraded model would be called the MacBook Ultra, but the fate of the MacBook Pro brand has been unclear. The picture is now much clearer.

[1] At first, everyone assumed the entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M5 chip would keep the MacBook Pro name. Then Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman reported that Apple would bring many elements of the MacBook Ultra design to the entry-level MacBook Pro with the M7 chip. In my view, this significantly reduces the chances of the 'MacBook Ultra' name being adopted.

[2] However, the latest reporting makes the idea of MacBook Pro and MacBook Ultra coexisting in the lineup far more plausible.

[3] According to Omdia, Apple will continue producing its existing miniLED display panels until 2028.

[4] This means two things: first, if the current MacBook Pro stays in the lineup, the new redesigned model will likely carry a significant price hike; at the same time, the new model will almost certainly be called the MacBook Ultra.

[5] So, for roughly the next year or so, the MacBook lineup will likely look something like this:

[6] Fall 2026:

  • [7] MacBook Neo (A18 Pro)
  • [8] MacBook Air (13-inch and 15-inch, M5)
  • [9] MacBook Pro (miniLED, 14-inch, M6)
  • [10] MacBook Pro (miniLED, 14-inch and 16-inch, M5 Pro and M5 Max)
  • [11] MacBook Ultra (OLED, 14-inch and 16-inch, M5 Pro and M5 Max)

[12] Spring 2027:

  • [13] MacBook Neo (A19 Pro)
  • [14] MacBook Air (13-inch and 15-inch, M6)
  • [15] MacBook Pro (OLED, 14-inch, M7)

[16] Wrap-up

[17] If all of this comes to pass, the MacBook lineup will be the largest ever. The older MacBook Pro is not expected to remain in the lineup for long. I suspect this is part of Apple's strategy of maintaining a lower starting price, consistent with what they've always done.

[18] In this scenario, I expect the miniLED MacBook Pro to start at around US$2,499, while the Ultra will start higher, possibly at US$2,999.

[19] What do you think of this rumoured MacBook lineup? What starting price do you expect for the MacBook Ultra? Let us know in the comments section.
